first_impression.summary_in_own_words: It's a guide to getting married in Portugal, broken down by region, with someone called a Wedded Advisor who can plan it for you. The headline 'Get Married in Portugal, from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff' is pretty and makes me picture it. But the first lines under it are about legal paperwork and a one month registry process, and there's deliberately no price anywhere up top. Portugal wasn't really on our list (we've been looking at Italy, Greece, Bali), so I'd keep scrolling out of curiosity, not because I'm sold.

attention_map.quote: Get Married in Portugal, from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff
attention_map.why: Palace or cliff is the kind of 'different, not a standard package' thing I want. But the quick answer goes straight into a civil process for foreign couples and 'at least one month before the date'. On my phone at 10pm I don't care about the registry yet. I want to know if we can afford it and fit our people.

attention_map.quote: many couples hold a symbolic ceremony in Portugal and marry legally at home
attention_map.why: This one line helps a lot. It tells me we don't have to sort out overseas paperwork. That takes some stress off straight away.

attention_map.quote: Which season are you planning for? ... How many guests? ... 'Check your date'
attention_map.why: Short and tapping on a phone is fine, it's not a long form. But it asks me for my guest count before the page has told me whether venues here can take 80 people. Feels like I'm handing over info to get a sales call.

attention_map.quote: a non-numeric line naming Wedded Concierge and one Wedded Advisor, or hide the strip
attention_map.why: If it's just a line with your own brand name on it, that tells me nothing. I'd scroll past.

attention_map.quote: Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue
attention_map.why: Pena palace, Douro terraces, sea stacks. Nice, and I'd stop if the photos are real and not stock. But it reads like a tourism guide. 'Ferdinand II' and 'Port regulated since 1756' is trivia, not wedding planning.

attention_map.quote: Setting; Best months; Nearest airport (code); Guests
attention_map.why: This is the bit I actually want: five regions, which airport we'd fly into. Then the guest line is blank or says 'Ask your Wedded Advisor'. That's the exact question I came with. Seeing a 'Guests' label with no answer is worse than leaving it off.

attention_map.quote: events on those dates may have to be cancelled ... roof restoration with scaffolding ... until Q1 2027
attention_map.why: Weirdly this makes me trust them more. Nobody else tells you the palace could be pulled for a state event or that there's scaffolding up. Also a bit scary. If we booked a palace and got cancelled, who sorts it out?

attention_map.quote: visa-free short stays on Australian, US and UK passports
attention_map.why: Good to know our guests won't need visas. The rest of the reasons cards repeat what I already scrolled past.

attention_map.quote: quinta; palace or pousada; clifftop or beach; vineyard estate; city palace; Catholic church
attention_map.why: Useful menu of options but no idea which of these suits 60 people or what each costs.

attention_map.quote: Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee
attention_map.why: This is exactly my worry about prices blowing out, and they're saying it out loud. I'd screenshot this for my partner. But with no numbers it just raises the worry without settling it.

attention_map.section: s5-plan (Entry rules and Marrying legally tabs)
attention_map.quote: Certificate of No Impediment (CNI) or registry certificates ... DFAT also issues CNIs in Australia
attention_map.why: Good that there's an Australian bit, and I'd come back to it on the weekend if we went legal. But US and UK sections, EES fingerprints, ETIAS, consular officers... on a phone this is a wall. I'd skip it tonight.

attention_map.quote: Fallback until then: explain what drives cost (guest count, region, season, nights at the venue, exclusivity) with no figures, and offer a Wedded Advisor estimate.
attention_map.why: If it goes live with the fallback, the page has no price at all. That's the thing that makes me close a tab. If the table does ship ('total EUR 25,000 to 70,000' for about 100 guests) I'd be really engaged, even in euros, because I could check it against our budget. Right now it's a maybe.

attention_map.quote: Venue nights with rooms, welcome dinner, ceremony, long dinner, late party, Sunday brunch, an on-the-day coordinator
attention_map.why: This is the picture I want: a whole weekend with our guests. It feels intimate and like us. But it's 'what a weekend can include', not what I'd get or for how much.

attention_map.quote: Quinta rooms first, then nearby hotels ... Transfers from Lisbon or Porto
attention_map.why: Answers where our guests stay and how they get there. No flight times from Australia though, and nothing on how long the transfer takes.
No real weddings in Portugal to look at. I want to see that someone like us has actually done this with you here.

attention_map.quote: one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend
attention_map.why: One person handling it across time zones is exactly what I want. But it's a job title, not a person. No name, no face, no idea what they do week to week or what they charge. 'A Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call' means I have to get on a call to find out the cost of the planner.

attention_map.quote: Is a wedding in Portugal cheaper than at home?
attention_map.why: I'd tap this one first. If the answer dodges with no comparison and no number, I'll feel fobbed off.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links. Not why I'm here, I'd ignore them.

questions_answered.question: What does this cost all in, and what is included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: 'No Wedded Wonderland figure and no 'From AUD' price on this page.' The only figures are a third party EUR range that is 'Apply only after sign-off'; the fallback has 'no figures'. s6 lists what a weekend 'can include' but not tied to any price.

questions_answered.question: Can it fit our guest count?
questions_answered.evidence: Region cards: 'Guests line: no sourced guest range exists. Leave it out of the cards (or 'Ask your Wedded Advisor')'. 'No named venue capacities'. The page asks for my guest count in the B9 bar but never tells me what fits.

questions_answered.question: Who would actually plan this with us, and what do they do?
questions_answered.evidence: 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' and a 'How it works' block. No named person, no photo, no fee line, founder quote removed.

questions_answered.question: How do our guests get there and where do they stay?
questions_answered.evidence: Airports LIS, OPO, FAO, FNC; 'Transfers from Lisbon or Porto'; 'Quinta rooms first, then nearby hotels'; visa-free on Australian passports. No flight or transfer times ('No flight times (none sourced)'), no hotel names.

questions_answered.question: Is our budget realistic for this place?
questions_answered.evidence: Only if the cost table ships: 'about 100 guests: total EUR 25,000 to 70,000'. With the fallback it is 'no'. Even with it, it's euros for 100 guests only; the 50 to 80 band 'not shown'.

objections_triggered.objection: Prices look like they start low and will blow out
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee; fees may be per day or per guest with a minimum' with no numbers next to it, and no From price.

objections_triggered.objection: I don't know if my budget is possible for this many people
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Guests line blank on every region card; cost table only for about 100 guests and possibly hidden behind 'Apply only after sign-off'.

objections_triggered.objection: Planning from overseas, time zones and suppliers I can't meet
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Partly calmed by 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend', but no named person and no explanation of how they work with us from Australia.

objections_triggered.objection: Every planner's page looks the same
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Palace and Douro spotlight reads like a tourism page; the palace rules strip and venue charges box are the only bits that feel different.

trust_signals_noticed: Travel info by airport code on every region card (LIS, FAO, OPO, FNC)
An Australian passport section and visa-free entry for Australians
Honest palace rules: state-event cancellations and Monserrate scaffolding until Q1 2027
Venue charges box warning about unoccupied rooms and buy-outs
'Legal and cost details checked October 2026, with sources named in each tab.'
One Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend (but unnamed)
turn_offs_noticed: No price signal at all if the Costs tab goes live with its no-figures fallback
Guests label on region cards with no answer
Guest count asked in the B9 bar before the page tells me what fits
Legal tabs covering US and UK passports too, long on mobile
Celebrity trending links at the bottom
No real weddings in Portugal shown

emotional_response.overall: Curious and a bit charmed by the palace and cliff idea, but still anxious about money and numbers. Feels careful and honest, not exciting.
moments_of_reassurance: symbolic ceremony here, legal at home
on-the-day coordinator and a planned weekend
moments_of_doubt: planner is a title, not a person

payload.decision_reason: I'd save it and send it to my partner because the weekend, guests and palace rules sections are genuinely useful and Portugal looks like something different. I wouldn't enquire. My three must-haves are missing: no From price with what's included, nothing telling me if venues fit our guest count, and no named person who'd plan it. If the cost table goes live with the no-figures fallback, the weekend read could easily turn into a leave.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Okay, a palace in Sintra or a cliff in the Algarve, that's cute and not the usual Italy thing. But babe, there's no price anywhere. There's a 'Guests' bit on each region and it's blank. They warn us about paying for empty rooms but don't say how much anything costs. The legal stuff is super long, though at least there's an Aussie bit. I like that one person plans it all, but who is it and what do they charge? Saving this, let's look properly on Saturday. Not filling in a form just to find out if 60 people and our budget even work.
